The word 'Sikh' means
x: The term 'Sikh' is derived from a Sanskrit/Pali word meaning 'disciple' or 'learner', reflecting the follower's relationship with the Sikh Gurus.

s: Which of the following was the birthplace of Guru Nanak?
x: Nankana Sahib is a city and capital of Nankana Sahib district in the Punjab province of Pakistan. Nankana was the birthplace of Guru Nanak, the founder of Sikh religion. He was born on April 15, 1469 AD, in a Khatri family. He had a strong faith in the worship of Nirakar Brahma. He passed away in 1539 AD at Derababa Nanak (Kartarpur Pakistan).

s: Who was the successor of Guru Nanak?
x: Guru Nanak chose Bhai Lehna, who became Guru Angad, as his successor before his death. Amar Das and Ram Das came later.

Who had Guru Nanak appointed his successor?

(d) 'Gurumukhi' originates from Punjabi word 'Gurumukha' that means – from the mouth of Guru. Gurumukhi script was started by second Sikh Guru, Guru Angad.

s: Which Sikh Guru was born in Patna?
x: Guru Gobind Singh was the tenth and the last Sikh Guru. He was born in 1666 A.D. in Patna (Bihar). He introduced ‘Khalsa Panth’ and consolidated the Sikh community as a warrior.

s: Who was the tenth (10th) Guru of the Sikhs?
x: Guru Gobind Singh was the tenth Sikh Guru; he founded the Khalsa Panth in 1699.

s:
Verses ascribed to poet-saint Kabir have been compiled in which of the following traditions?

I. Bijak in Varanasi

II. Kabir Granthavali in Rajasthan

III. Adi Granth Sahib
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
x: Kabir's work Bijak is linked to his followers, and the Adi Granth/Guru Granth Sahib contains his verses. The Kabir Granthavali tradition in Rajasthan is not in the notes, but all three options are accepted as correct, so 'All of these' is right.

s: Under which Sikh Guru, the Sikhs were transformed into the 'Khalsa'?
x: Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa in 1699 and made the Sikhs a military order. The other Gurus did not found it.

s: Guru Gobind Singh’s greatness lies in the fact that :
o: He formed the military order of Sikhs
He was the founder of Sikh state
x: The 10th Guru and last prophet of Sikhism, Guru Gobind Singh converted Sikhs into a military sect ‘‘Khalsa Panth’’. He called the whole Sikh community as ‘‘Khalsa’’. He ordered Sikhs that each Sikh should have the surname of 'Singh' (male) and 'Kaur' (female) and should hold 5 k's- Kesh, Kangha, Kachha, Kripan and Kada.

s: In which year did Guru Govind Singh found ‘Khalsa’?
x: Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa on Baisakhi, 13 April 1699, at Anandpur.

s: Guru Gobind Singh greatness lies in the fact that
o: he formed the military order of Sikh.
he was the founder of Sikh state.
x: Guru Gobind Singh made the Sikhs a military order through the Khalsa (Singh/Kaur surnames, Five Ks). He did not found the Sikh state (that was Banda Bahadur) and did not make Sikhs peaceful.

s: How many years ago Khalsa Panth started?
x: Khalsa Panth was established on 13th April, 1699, on the day of Baisakhi by 10th Sikh Guru Gobind Singh in Anandpur Sahib. Therefore, it has been more than 300 years since Khalsa Panth started.

s: The Guru who founded the ‘Khalsa’ was :
x: The Khalsa was founded by the tenth Guru, Gobind Singh, in 1699. Har Rai, Har Kishan and Tegh Bahadur preceded him.

s: Which among the following Sikh Gurus instituted the Khalsa Panth?
x: Guru Gobind Singh instituted the Khalsa Panth on Baisakhi 1699 at Anandpur.

s: The Sikh Guru executed by the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb was
x: Guru Tegh Bahadur was executed by Aurangzeb at Delhi in 1675. Arjan Dev was executed under Jahangir.

s: Aurangzeb is responsible for which Sikh prophet’s death?
x: Aurangzeb executed Guru Tegh Bahadur at Delhi in 1675.

s: Who was the Sikh Guru to be slaughtered by Aurangzeb?
x: Tegh Bahadur was executed by Aurangzeb in 1675. Arjan Dev was executed under Jahangir instead.

s: Which Sikh Guru was publicly killed by Aurangzeb in 1675 for not embracing Islam?
x: Guru Tegh Bahadur was executed by Aurangzeb at Delhi in 1675. Arjan Dev died under Jahangir in 1606.

s:
Which of the following Sikh Gurus were penalised with death by the Rulers of the time?

I. Guru Angad

II. Guru Arjan Dev

III. Guru Har Gobind

IV. Guru Tegh Bahadur
Select the correct answer from the codes given below.
x: Arjan Dev was executed by Jahangir (1606) and Tegh Bahadur by Aurangzeb (1675). Hargobind was only imprisoned and freed, and Angad was not executed.

s: To which Sikh Guru, Akbar donated 500 Bighas of land?
x: Akbar granted 500 bighas of land to the fourth Guru, Ram Das, where Ramdaspur (Amritsar) was founded.

s: The Sikh Guru who completed the construction of the Golden Temple in Amritsar was:
x: While Guru Ram Das founded Amritsar, his successor Guru Arjun Dev completed the Harmandir Sahib and installed the Adi Granth there.

s: The city of Amritsar in Punjab was established by:
x: Gazzetteer of Amritsar district, mentions that the fourth Guru Ramdas obtained from Akbar the grant of piece of land (around 500 bighas) on the spot where now stands the city of Amritsar and dug the holy tank, and commenced the erection of a temple in its midst. Some sources also state that it was gifted to Bibi Bhani (wife of Guru Ramdas) by Akbar. Ramdas died in 1581 A.D. and his son & successor, Guru Arjan completed the temple.

s: Which of the following is the birth place of Guru Nanak?
x: Guru Nanak was born in 1469 at Talwandi (Nankana Sahib) near the Ravi, so Talwandi is correct; Amritsar was founded later by Guru Ram Das.

s: Nanded is considered sacred by Sikhs due to whose Mausoleum?
x: The 10th Sikh Guru and last Guru, Guru Gobind Singh was assassinated in Nanded (Maharashtra) by an Afghani noble. 'Takhat Sachkhand Sri Hazur Abchalnagar Sahib' Gurudwara of Nanded is situated at his cremation site.

s: Which of the following cities was the capital of Maharaja Ranjit Singh?
Capital of Kingdom of Maharaja Ranjit Singh was:
x: Zaman Shah invaded Punjab in 1798 AD. While returning, his cannons had fallen in the Jhelum River. Ranjit Singh returned them safely to Lahore. In 1799 AD, he seized Lahore and made it capital. 5. At which place did Raja Ranjit Singh set up the Adalati-Ala? (a) Amritsar (b) Lahore (c) Firozpur (d) Multan U.P.P.C.S. (Pre.) 2021 Ans (b) Maharaja Ranjit Singh set up the Adalat-i-Ala at Lahore which heard appeals from the district and provincial courts. 6. The Treaty of Amritsar was concluded between Maharaja Ranjit Singh and (a) Lord Cornwallis (b) Lord Dalhousie (c) Lord Hastings (d) Lord Minto Jharkhand P.C.S. (Pre) 2023 Ans. (d) Treaty of Amritsar was signed by Mr. Charles Metcalfe on behalf of British Governor general Lord Minto I and Maharaja Ranjit Singh at Amritsar on April 25, 1809 AD. According to this treaty, Ranjit Singh was to recognize the river Sutlej as the boundary and to accept the British suzerainty over his vassals across the river, and the English were to recognize the Maharaja as the sole sovereign on his side of River Sutlej.

s: Who among the following has said, ‘God intended me to look upon all religions with one eye, that is why he took away the light from the other’?
x: The above statement was made by Maharaja Ranjit Singh. Ranjit Singh was born on 13 Nov. 1780 A.D. at Gujranwala. When he was only 12 years old, his father Maha Singh died. A council of regency governed administration from 1792 A.D. to 1797 A.D. which included his mother, mother-in-Law and Diwan Lakhpat Rai. He assumed the powers directly in 1797. Ranjit Singh annexed Lahore (1799 A.D.), Amritsar (1802 A.D.). 9. Which of the following statements is/are correct in the context of the Treaty of Lahore (1846)? I. The Maharaja left all his territories beyond the river Satluj forever. II. The Maharaja left his rights over all the forts between the Satluj and Beas rivers in favour of the Company. III. The English army could no longer pass through the Sikh State. Select the correct answer from the codes given below : (a) Only II and III (b) Only I and II (c) I, II and III (d) Only I U.P. R.O/A.R.O (Re. Exam) (Pre) 2025 Ans. (b) The British army occupied Lahore and in March 1846, forced the Sikhs to sign the Treaty of Lahore with following terms – – The Maharaja, ceded all his territories across the Sutlej river forever. – Maharaja completely relinquished his control over all the forts situated between Sutlej & Beas Rivers in favour of company. – They promised not to interfere in the administration. – The Sikhs were required to pay one and a half crore ruppes as war indemnity etc.

s: Who is the author of the book, “Landmarks in Indian Constitutional and National Development”?
x: The book “Landmarks in Indian Constitution and National Development” is a masterpiece of Gurmukh Nihal Singh. He also served as the first Governor of Rajasthan from 1956 to 1962.

s: To which Misl did Ranjeet Singh belong:
x: Ranjit Singh was born on 13 November, 1780 in the home of Maha Singh, the chief of Sukerchakia Misl. On 25th April 1809, the treaty of Amritsar took place between Maharaja Ranjit Singh and British. The terms of the treaty prevented Singh from any further territorial expansion south of the Sutlej but on the other hand, as Cunningham said, Ranjit Singh occupied authority to spread kingdom in the West. He annexed Multan (1818), Kashmir (1819) and Peshawar Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (1834). Thus, among given options, Sri Nagar was included in the kingdom of Ranjit Singh.

s: Maharaja Ranjit Singh made his political and religious capital to
x: Ranjit Singh captured Lahore in 1799 and made it his capital, while Amritsar was the Sikh religious centre (Golden Temple). So Lahore, Amritsar fits; the notes do not directly state Amritsar's religious-capital role beyond the Golden Temple link.

s: Who has conferred the title of ‘Raja’ to Ranjit Singh?

s: Ranjit Singh was related to which Misl?

s: Which of the following was included in the Maharaja Ranjit Singh empire?
x: Srinagar (Kashmir) was annexed by Ranjit Singh in 1819, so it was in his empire; Delhi, Kabul and Makrana were not.

s: Who was the successor of Maharaja Ranjit Singh?
x: After Ranjit Singh died in 1839, his son Kharak Singh succeeded him; Sher Singh and Nau Nihal Singh came later.
